groups.title: Testing Django and React
groups.question: You need tests for your Django API and your React components before releasing. Explain how you would test each and fake the API in frontend tests.

followUps.Django Testing with pytest and pytest-dj: What does pytest-django give you for testing the API?
followUps.React Component Testing with Vitest: How would you test a React component with Vitest and Testing Library?
followUps.Mocking API Calls with MSW: How does MSW fake API calls in tests?

evidence.text: pytest-django provides fixtures like database access and a test client.
APIClient sends authenticated requests to DRF endpoints.
Tests check status codes, data and permission rules.
Vitest runs fast and shares the Vite configuration.
Testing Library renders the component.
Tests assert on what the user sees rather than internal details.

notEnough: Only saying you write component tests.

evidence.text: Mock Service Worker intercepts network requests.
Components run their real fetching code against fake responses.
The same handlers work in tests and during development.

notEnough: Only saying MSW mocks the API.

groups.title: Containerization
groups.question: You are packaging the Django API, the React build, Postgres, Redis and Nginx to run together. Explain how you would containerise the stack and handle secrets.

followUps.Dockerizing Django and React: How would you containerise Django and React?
followUps.Environment Variables and Secrets in Doc: How should secrets be passed to containers?

evidence.text: A multi-stage Dockerfile builds React and keeps only the static output.
Django runs in its own image with Gunicorn.
Docker Compose runs the app, database, Redis and Nginx together.
Secrets are passed as environment variables, not baked into images.
.env files with secrets are not committed.
In production a secrets manager or the platform's secret store is used.

notEnough: Only saying you use environment variables.

groups.title: Production Serving
groups.question: In production, Django should not serve static files or face the internet directly. Explain how Gunicorn and Nginx serve the app.

followUps.Gunicorn WSGI Server Configuration: What does Gunicorn do, and how do you choose the number of workers?
followUps.Nginx as Reverse Proxy and Static Server: What does Nginx do in front of Django?

evidence.text: Gunicorn is a production server that runs the Django app.
It runs several worker processes, often about two per CPU core plus one.
It runs behind a reverse proxy rather than facing the internet directly.
Nginx serves static files and the React build directly.
It forwards API requests to Gunicorn.
Python never handles static file requests, which is faster.

notEnough: Only saying Nginx is a web server.

groups.title: Cloud Deployment
groups.question: You are deploying to a cloud platform and want the simplest setup for static files. Explain how you would prepare and deploy the app.

followUps.collectstatic and WhiteNoise for Static: What do collectstatic and WhiteNoise do?
followUps.Deploying to a Cloud Platform: What would you weigh when choosing between a platform like Render and AWS?

evidence.text: collectstatic gathers all static files into one folder.
WhiteNoise lets Django serve those files efficiently, compressed and cached.
This avoids needing a separate static server or CDN at first.

notEnough: Only saying it handles static files.

evidence.text: Platforms like Railway, Render or Fly.io deploy containers with little setup.
AWS services like ECS, RDS and ElastiCache give more control and scale.
The trade-off is simplicity and speed against flexibility and operational work.
